public_rationale: This is a conditional forecast with no deadline. Under the contract's reading, it applies only if an AI data center tenant whose payments back the debt fails to pay. A tracker of GPU and data center credit events, available October 17, 2026, says no neocloud had publicly defaulted on a GPU-backed loan as of October 2026, and it found no public record of such a loan being foreclosed (e1). The same tracker lists AI companies that stopped paying for compute or filed, including Stability AI and Character.AI (e1). Under the contract's reading, those compute buyers are not data center tenants. The packet does not show a qualifying tenant payment failure, or any of the later steps in the predicted chain. So the forecast cannot be scored yet.
limitations: The evidence on the condition comes from one secondary tracker, not a full search of court, filing and lender records.
The tracker's statement covers GPU-backed loan defaults by neoclouds, which is narrower than every way a data center tenant could fail to pay.
The tracker was available October 17, 2026, so it may not cover the days up to the October 28 evaluation date.
Private or unreported payment failures would not appear in the evidence.
Under a broader reading of 'customer' that includes indirect compute buyers, the Character.AI filing could count. The contract uses the narrower tenant reading.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: If one AI data center customer can't pay, other customers can't pay, and that will mean less demand for AI data centers, a glut of data center infrastructure, and resale assets that won't be worth as much.

statement.excerpt: For whatever reason, nobody wants to consider the most obvious problem: that if one customer can’t pay, other customers can’t pay, and if other customers can’t pay, there’s going to be less demand for AI data centers in general, which means there will be a glut of data center infrastructure, which will mean those assets you intend to resell if everything goes poorly won’t be worth as much.

from_speaker: less demand for AI data centers in general
a glut of data center infrastructure
those assets you intend to resell ... won't be worth as much
our_interpretation: In context, 'customer' means a tenant of an AI data center whose lease payments back data-center bonds or loans (for example a lab, hyperscaler or neocloud leasing capacity). It does not mean any company that buys cloud compute indirectly.
The antecedent is met only if such a tenant publicly fails to pay its data center obligations (missed lease payments, default, or bankruptcy that stops payment).
Only if that happens can the chain be scored: other tenants failing to pay, falling demand, a capacity glut, and lower resale values for data center assets.
No deadline is stated, so this is an open conditional.
criteria.support_condition: After a data center tenant fails to pay, public records show other tenants also failing to pay, falling demand or rising vacancy for AI data center capacity, and lower resale or collateral values for data center assets.
criteria.contradiction_condition: After a data center tenant fails to pay, other tenants keep paying, demand for AI data center capacity holds, and the affected assets are re-leased or sold without a material loss in value.

evidence.explanation: As of October 2026 the tracker records no neocloud default and no data center tenant failing to pay in 2026. The 2026 entries are a cloud-compute buyer's bankruptcy and lease walkaways that were not defaults. So the antecedent had not happened by the time of the post.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: A dated public failure by an AI data center tenant to pay its lease or capacity obligations. After that, evidence on whether other tenants kept paying, on AI data center vacancy and demand, and on resale or collateral values for the affected assets.
